title: {Syn} Dijkstra Algorithm Greedily Finds Shortest Paths
content:
Dijkstra algorithm finds shortest paths from one source in a graph with nonnegative edge weights. It repeatedly settles the nearest unsettled vertex.

The nonnegative condition matters. With negative edges, a later path can undercut a distance that looked final, which is why Bellman-Ford exists.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
